correctness.rationale: For all finite simple labeled K_{p,q}-ab (p,q>=2), every three-edge geodesic joins the missing endpoints and is a-x-y-b. Thus an edge subset with i selected left spokes and j right spokes excludes precisely ij rectangle middle edges, yielding E. Maximality forces every permissible middle edge; the exact alternatives are i,j>=1, i=t,j=0, or i=0,j=s. This gives M and the cardinality gap. Independent BFS-and-all-subsets verification passed all nine small parameter pairs, including 4x5 (164305 admissible edge subsets); the infinite theorem is proven by classification, not by sampling.

value.rationale: Deleting one edge is a natural sharp perturbation of a diameter-two graph whose edge-general-position complex is a simplex. The theorem supplies two complete infinite-family counting polynomials, exact inclusion-maximal enumeration, minimum/maximum facet cardinalities, and arbitrarily long omissions in the facet-size spectrum; this exposes genuine non-purity/lacunarity not implied by a scalar optimum.
